summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with fever, cough with hemoptysis, and dysuria. Evaluation revealed a urinary tract infection with positive nitrites and leukocytes in urine; a CT scan of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis showed no pneumonia or nephrolithiasis but revealed chronic atelectasis in the left upper lobe. She was treated with levofloxacin for both suspected bacterial bronchitis and UTI. Her cardiac status was stable with normal proBNP and no signs of fluid overload, so the evening dose of furosemide was held. Oxygen was provided overnight due to obstructive sleep apnea and pulmonary hypertension. She was counseled on hygiene practices to reduce UTI recurrence, prescribed vaginal estrogen cream, and advised to follow up with urology. She remained afebrile, improved symptomatically, and was discharged home with instructions to complete antibiotics, monitor weight, and seek care if fever or respiratory symptoms returned.
